questions.key_step: Spot that g(x)->1 from the left on both sides, so only f(1-) matters.
questions.justification: One familiar move (one-sided limit of a composite) but with a small trap about f(1)=4; same single-move demand as the 1^infinity limit.

questions.key_step: Only cos x is even, so its coefficient is killed; then f' >= 0 forces b >= 1.
questions.justification: Routine chain: oddness, factor a quadratic, derivative sign with a growth argument for b<1; no hidden idea.

questions.key_step: Fundamental period 6, then count many-one as total minus injective.
questions.justification: Two linked ideas (period of a sum of modulus trig terms; counting with order conditions and complement). Format SCQ lowers it relative to a numerical.

questions.key_step: g -> 2 from the left; evaluate [t], sgn(sin pi t) and tan(pi t)/(t-2) at 2-.
questions.justification: Several one-sided evaluations chained (half-angle, GIF, signum, tan periodicity); precision on the side of approach.

questions.key_step: Range by discriminant, f decreasing so bijective, and f=f^-1 reduces to x^3+2x-1=0 by IVT.
questions.justification: Four statements each needing a genuine check (range, bijection/inverse, number of solutions of f=f^-1 on the common domain); multi-concept (range, inverse, IVT).

questions.key_step: Resolve max/min into polynomials; corners at -1 and 1 always, at 0 only if b-a=2.
questions.justification: Four statements with parameter dependence and IVT; closest to the max/min piecewise anchor 2023-P2-Q6.

questions.key_step: Running maximum is flat until sqrt3; check slopes at sqrt3 and 2, count roots of f=2x, IVT range check.
questions.justification: Understanding the running-maximum function is the key; four verifiable statements, moderate computation.

questions.key_step: Series coefficients decide finite limit and type of discontinuity.
questions.justification: Four statements, each a parameter-limit with series expansion and classification of discontinuity; routine but long.

questions.key_step: Each derivative lowers the exponent by n+1; compare with the thresholds.
questions.justification: General x^m sin(x^-n) family needs the exponent-counting idea; for n=2 and k=2 it is two thresholds.

questions.key_step: Convert g'' to f''' and test thresholds for k=3 and k=4 at m=7, borderline case.
questions.justification: Same machinery as Q9 but deeper (k=3, 4) with a borderline value where one oscillates; four statements with one subtle borderline.

questions.key_step: k^4+k^2+2 = 1+(k^2+k+1)(k^2-k+1) telescopes the arctans; tail via cot^-1.
questions.justification: Known factorisation trick then a standard limit; numerical format (no options). Same telescoping idea as 2021-P1-Q15.

questions.key_step: Nested modulus zig-zag: five corners at 0,1,2,3,4 and area of two triangles.
questions.justification: Routine multi-step: simplify the composition, find corners, add areas; no insight beyond care with the nested modulus.

questions.key_step: Convert conditions (i), (ii), (iii) into empty Venn regions, leaving three regions to fill.
questions.justification: Three set conditions to decode into regions with careful casework; a slip changes the count and there are no options.

questions.key_step: Reflexive-symmetric relations are 2^3=8 and 5 are equivalence relations.
questions.justification: Short chain on equivalence-relation counting; the +0.5 equivalence adjustment applies, integer level kept at 2.

questions.key_step: R o R^-1 is symmetric so R is symmetric, then transitive; count equivalence relations.
questions.justification: Composition of relations is an unfamiliar element plus the equivalence-relation decoding; short once seen.

questions.key_step: Add the arctans with the tan addition formula and convert sin^-1 to tan^-1.
questions.justification: Routine ITF chain: evaluate two terms, add, subtract from pi/4, solve; no hidden idea.

questions.key_step: The 1^infinity limit gives f(a)=exp((a^4-4a^2)/2); classes are the fibres of f.
questions.justification: Standard 1^infinity limit plus reading equivalence classes from a function; short, adjustment +0.5 applies.
